video.title: JPY Structural Recovery & Double-Dip Strategy Overview

thesis_health.reason: BOJ hikes benchmark rate to 31-year high of 1.25% while FOMC lifts to 3.75%-4.00%, preserving bilateral spread cushion.

scenarios.description: BOJ accelerates tightening past 1.50% into 2027 while Fed pauses; Shunto wage rounds remain above 4.5%; Prime Market buyback announcements exceed ¥16 trillion annualized; mega-bank domestic NIM surges >35 bps.

BOJ maintains 1.25% with gradual glide path to 1.50%; FOMC at 3.75%-4.00% preserves 250-275 bps spread, keeping USD/JPY in the 148-158 corridor; mega-banks and non-life insurers sustain 10.5%-11.5% ROE alongside steady buybacks.
entry_conditions: Domestic NIM expands 20-25 bps on sticky deposits
exit_conditions: Domestic commercial credit costs exceed 50 bps

scenarios.description: Severe global recession forces synchronized central bank easing; aggressive risk-off carry unwind collapses USD/JPY below 125, compressing multinational translation profits while domestic SME insolvencies climb.
exit_conditions: Widespread reversal of corporate buyback commitments

decision.summary: The double-dip thesis is reinforced: the BOJ's September 18 hike to 1.25% unlocks incremental domestic NIM expansion, while the Fed's 25 bps hike to 3.75%-4.00% protects overseas lending margins and shields exporters from translation shock. Maintain active buy on MUFG and SMFG.
required_actions: Accumulate MUFG below attractive entry limit of ¥1,850/share
Monitor corporate loan yield resets following the September 24 effective date for the 1.25% rate
Audit Q2 cross-holding liquidation volume for SMFG and Tokio Marine in November

developments.title: Bank of Japan Raises Policy Rate to 31-Year High of 1.25%
developments.fact: The BOJ Policy Board voted 7-2 on September 18, 2026, to raise the uncollateralized overnight call rate by 25 bps from 1.00% to 1.25% (effective September 24), citing core CPI near 2% and persistent wage-price transmission.
developments.interpretation: Directly expands domestic loan asset yields across floating corporate and retail portfolios while domestic deposit costs remain pinned near zero.

developments.title: FOMC Raises Federal Funds Rate to 3.75%-4.00%, Preserving 250-275 bps Yield Spread
developments.fact: The Federal Reserve lifted the target range for the federal funds rate by 25 bps to 3.75%-4.00% on September 16, 2026, keeping the short-term US-Japan rate differential wide at ~260 bps.
developments.interpretation: Prevents disruptive yen appreciation below 135/USD, sustaining translated foreign cash flows for Japanese exporters and bolstering USD asset returns at mega-banks.

developments.title: Japanese Mega-Banks Deliver Record Combined FY Net Income of ¥5.26 Trillion
developments.fact: MUFG, SMFG, and Mizuho reported aggregate full-year net profit of ¥5.26 trillion (+34% YoY), with MUFG ROE reaching 11.3% and SMFG achieving 10.4%.
developments.interpretation: Confirms the asymmetric operating leverage of massive deposit bases during an active central bank tightening regime.

developments.title: SMFG Executes Accelerated ¥180B Buyback and Advances Strategic Unwinding
developments.fact: SMFG completed ¥108.5B of share repurchases through June 30, 2026, targeting full completion of its ¥180B authorization while reducing strategic equity holdings toward <14% of CET1 by 2027.
developments.interpretation: Demonstrates structural capital recycling where cross-shareholding divestments are directly converted into EPS-accretive share cancellations.

developments.title: Tokio Marine Pledges Accelerated Complete Unwinding of ¥3.4T Cross-Holdings
developments.fact: Tokio Marine Holdings committed to liquidating its entire ¥3.4 trillion strategic equity portfolio to zero within 4-5 years, deploying proceeds into annual buybacks of ¥150-¥200B while reinvesting float into higher-yielding JGBs.
developments.interpretation: Replaces volatile corporate equity holdings with recurring 1.25%+ fixed-income yields, funding consistent share retirement.

developments.title: Tokyo Stock Exchange Prime Market P/B Compliance Reaches 78%
developments.fact: 78% of Prime Market listed companies trading below 1.0x book value have published capital efficiency roadmaps, expanding average TOPIX payout ratios to 41.5%.
developments.interpretation: Confirms governance reform is an institutionalized, systemic transformation across corporate Japan.

developments.title: Valuation Dislocation Restricts Premium Automation and Tech Exporters
developments.fact: Keyence trades at 34.5x forward EPS amid softening global capex cycles, underscoring the necessity of valuation discipline in routing capital exclusively to sub-1.0x P/B financials.
developments.interpretation: Validates the portfolio strategy of prioritizing discounted financial compounders over multiple-stretched exporters.

scorecard.name: Monetary Policy Normalization & Yield Curve Shift
scorecard.assessment: Policy rate raised to 1.25% on September 18, 2026; 10-year JGB yield firmly anchored above 1.20% as NIRP era is definitively closed.

scorecard.name: Domestic Banking NIM & Cash Flow Leverage
scorecard.assessment: Deposit beta remains under 8% while commercial loan yields adjust upward with the 1.25% benchmark; combined net profits tracking above ¥5.26T.

scorecard.name: TSE Governance Revolution & P/B Target Compliance
scorecard.assessment: 78% compliance across Prime Market companies; strategic cross-shareholdings are being dissolved on legally committed timetables.

scorecard.name: Capital Return Acceleration (Buybacks & Dividend Resets)
scorecard.assessment: Market-wide buybacks tracking >¥12 trillion annually; dividend payout ratios expanding toward 40%-50% benchmarks.

scorecard.name: Wage-Price Virtuous Cycle & Domestic Reflation
scorecard.assessment: Sustained nominal wage growth of 4.7% supports stable core inflation near 2.0%, avoiding domestic purchasing power collapse.

scorecard.name: Global Cash Flow Moats vs Foreign Exchange Translation
scorecard.assessment: USD/JPY supported at 155-157 range prevents near-term export earnings erosion, though multiple discipline remains critical.

scorecard.name: Bilateral Policy Differential & Carry Trade Cushion
scorecard.assessment: Fed hike to 3.75%-4.00% and BOJ hike to 1.25% maintain a 250-275 bps spread, avoiding a disorderly carry trade collapse.

assumptions_changed.reason: Empirical confirmation of FOMC rate hike to 3.75%-4.00% alongside BOJ hike to 1.25% establishes a predictable bilateral spread corridor.

publication.headline: BOJ Hikes Benchmark Rate to 31-Year High of 1.25% as Fed Tightening Secures Double-Dip Thesis
publication.summary: The Bank of Japan lifted its policy rate to 1.25% on September 18, accelerating domestic bank net interest margin expansion. Concurrently, the Federal Reserve's rate hike to 3.75%-4.00% preserves a wide yield differential, sheltering Japanese exporters from translation drag while corporate governance buybacks surge.
